subject: Azure Private Plan — commercial routing, co-sell split & SLA feedback
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Azure private plan — initial ask from Mediq (routing + SLA concerns)

Marissa / Irene —

I had a 30-minute call with Liam and Alicia from Mediq this morning. They want to proceed with an Azure Private Plan but flagged two items we need to align on before legal will accept:

1) Billing / procurement routing: they need the invoice to be payable to their US entity but with marketplace entitlement tied to the private plan SKU so their Azure PO flows correctly. Their procurement contact (procurement@mediqhealth.com) is explicit that vendor invoices must reference the Marketplace Offer ID.

2) SLA & credits: their procurement team is asking for a stronger credit schedule for the Service Level than our standard Marketplace exhibit — specifically, earlier crediting for <99.9% and a faster claims resolution timeline. They said this is a hard stop for Finance unless we can offer a localized SLA addendum.

I attached the short notes from the call. Can you review and advise what flex we have on (A) the invoice reference language that still satisfies Azure listing rules, and (B) SLA credit exposure on a private plan? If needed, I can loop in legal but want to raise it here first.

Also — they asked about co-sell revenue split expectations for listing with a Microsoft referral (they expect us to carry standard marketplace analytics routing). They suggested a 70/30 split in favor of Mediq if they introduce additional seats as an enterprise reseller; we should decide whether to accept that in a carve-out or keep marketplace revenue terms as-is.

Thanks,
Sergio
Head of Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Mediq_call_notes_20270110.txt (stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Azure private plan — initial ask from Mediq (routing + SLA concerns)

Thanks for the context, Serg. Quick notes from my side: 

- Billing language: we can include the Azure Offer ID on the invoice as a referenced field (e.g., "Azure Offer ID: 9f3b-priv-2027 / SKU PM-7892") without changing marketplace entitlement behavior. That typically satisfies procurement teams.
- SLA: Standard Azure private plan exhibit caps credits to 5% monthly for <99.9%. Mediq wants earlier tiering (e.g., credits starting at <99.95) which materially increases our exposure. We could offer a narrow addendum limited to the private plan and capped at 2% per month, with a faster response window (48 hrs for acknowledgment, 10 business days for remediation update). Legal will need to sign off.
- Co-sell split: 70/30 is unusual; our standard is 80/20 to partners on referral introductions where the partner handles onboarding. We can be flexible if Mediq commits to a revenue threshold (e.g., >$100k ARR) and takes a portion of onboarding costs. 

I'll draft a short commercial note and SOW bullet points for Irene to review with legal.

—Marissa
Director, Marketplace Partnerships
Attachment: commercial_summary_20270111.md (stub)

From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@mediqhealth.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@mediqhealth.com>, procurement@mediqhealth.com
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Azure private plan — initial ask from Mediq (routing + SLA concerns)

Sergio / Marissa —

Thanks for the quick follow-up. I've attached our procurement redlines and a clean PO template. High level:

- We need the invoice to reference the marketplace offer ID and the customer tenant ID. Example: "Azure Offer 9f3b-priv-2027; Tenant: mediq-prod-01".
- SLA: we can accept a capped credit exposure but need the first credit tier to start at <99.95% and to have a 30-day SLA claim window (procurement insists on this for internal auditing).
- Co-sell / reseller split: Mediq is open to a 70/30 split for ARR introduced by our sales team if Redwood covers first-line support for onboarding. If Redwood prefers 80/20, we can consider an implementation fee to bridge the gap.

Attached: Mediq_Azure_PrivatePlan_Redlines_20270112.pdf and PO_template_MediQ.pdf

Please review and propose language for the invoice reference and our SLA addendum. Liam and I can take a quick call Thursday if that helps.

Best,
Alicia Gomez
Head of Partnerships, Mediq Health

Attachment: Mediq_Azure_PrivatePlan_Redlines_20270112.pdf (actual redlines attached)

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Jan 2027 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Azure private plan — initial ask from Mediq (routing + SLA concerns)

Team —

I reviewed Mediq's redlines. Key legal positions I recommend we take:

1) Invoice reference: we can accept the Offer ID + Tenant ID on invoices as a stated reference, but we must include a clause in the SOW clarifying that the marketplace entitlement remains governed by Azure's commercial framework. Wording proposal: "Invoices payable to Mediq Health LLC will reference Azure Offer ID 9f3b-priv-2027 and Tenant mediq-prod-01 for procurement routing; such reference does not modify entitlement or billing flow controlled by Microsoft Marketplace policies."

2) SLA credits: do not accept tiering that starts at <99.95% without a strict cap. Proposed compromise: credits start at <99.9% per month, with a capped credit of 2% for the private plan on the first year, decreasing to 1% after year one. For claims: 30-day submission window is acceptable if claims are supported by Azure Marketplace incident logs; we cannot accept extended open-ended forensic obligations.

3) Co-sell split: accept a temporary 75/25 split in favor of Mediq for the first 12 months if Mediq guarantees >$120k ARR in that period and signs a reseller addendum that commits them to first-line onboarding support plus a reduced implementation fee. Otherwise revert to 80/20.

I'll prepare redline language and align with Finance (Markus) on credit exposure.

Irene
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed_sla_addendum_20270113.docx (stub)

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Jan 2027 11:41:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Azure private plan — commercial terms and credit exposure

Irene — good framing. From a finance perspective:

- Credit cap at 2% for year one is fine provided we include a strict cumulative cap per rolling 12 months and require claims to be tied to Azure Marketplace incident IDs. We should also require that Mediq's claims be prioritized through a single billing contact and that they commit to a 30-day contest period for disputed credits.
- On co-sell split, I support the 75/25 temporary carve-out (conditional on the ARR guarantee). We need an explicit recovery clause if Mediq cancels early (pro rata repayment of implementation subsidy).

If Irene finalizes language, I can sign off and Marissa can propose to Mediq. Recommend we keep PoC billing on monthly invoices but switch to quarterly invoicing once ARR > $50k/month to reduce processing overhead.

-Markus
VP Finance, Redwood Inference

Attachment: finance_note_credit_model_20270115.xlsx (stub)

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@mediqhealth.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@mediqhealth.com>, procurement@mediqhealth.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Azure private plan — commercial routing, co-sell split & SLA feedback

Alicia / Liam —

Thanks for the redlines and the quick turnaround. We reviewed internally and propose the following consolidated positions:

1) Invoice routing: Redwood will include the Azure Offer ID (9f3b-priv-2027) and your tenant identifier on all invoices as a procurement reference field. We'll add the SOW clarification that this reference does not alter Azure-managed entitlements.

2) SLA: We will provide a private-plan addendum that: starts crediting at <99.9% with a capped exposure of 2% for the first 12 months (cumulative 12-month cap applies), allows a 30-day claim submission window provided claims reference Azure Marketplace incident IDs, and commits to a 10-business-day initial remediation update after claim receipt. After 12 months, the cap reverts to 1% unless renegotiated.

3) Co-sell / reseller split: We can offer a 75/25 split in favor of Mediq for the first 12 months if Mediq signs the reseller addendum and guarantees $120k ARR in that period. If the ARR threshold is not met, terms revert to our standard 80/20. We request Mediq accept a one-time implementation subsidy from Redwood that would be recovered pro rata if the reseller relationship terminates within the first 12 months.

Next steps: Irene will send redline language for the SOW + SLA addendum and Markus will attach the finance exhibit for credit mechanics. If Mediq is good with this, Marissa will send a DocuSign SOW and we can move to PO routing. Can you confirm availability for a 20-minute call on Wednesday 1/20 to lock this?

Regards,
Sergio Alvarez
Head of Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachment: SOW-draft-MediQ-20270115.docx (attached)
